name: matrix_scene_s08_bridge_guard_20f
description: Twenty-frame Matrix 08 numerical-regression guard window for V5 native bridge performance work. The window lies strictly inside the reviewed actual shot Matrix-08-02 [73295, 73434) and is a centred subset of the already accepted matrix_scene_s08_30f window [73352, 73382), so it never crosses a verified cut.
om: G:\Filmy\IMAX format (open matte)\The Matrix (1999) [OPEN MATTE] [WEB-DL 1080p 10bit DD5.1 x265].mkv

legacy_sync.frame_rounding: inherited from the P2.34 anchor, not recomputed

guard_contract.purpose: before/after P010 plane comparison for the yuv_to_working_rgb performance fix
guard_contract.comparison_point: pre-NVENC GPU P010 buffers for every frame, compared in process
guard_contract.encoded_output: not produced; the Matrix HDR source exposes no Mastering display or Content light level side data, so the production Phase 2 NVENC/HDR10 remux path refuses this material
guard_contract.acceptance: max abs 10-bit code difference 0 across Y, U and V planes; a systematic shift is a regression

limitations: Synchronization and geometry are inherited from the P2.34 anchor and are not revalidated here.
Scene independence was never verified for this stratum (p2_32_scene_independence_verified is false).
The window is a bounded 20-frame guard sample inside one reviewed actual shot, not the whole shot and not a Phase 16 train/holdout benchmark.
The Open Matte source stream is HEVC, so the h264_cuvid default must be overridden with hevc_cuvid.
